evan: odd edge-case in Go generator streaming ergonomics. small repro shows Next() can block forever when caller cancels ctx during auth-refresh/backoff. filing to discuss API fixes and sample app guidance.

ev an: repro: start Stream(ctx), cancel ctx after first token; sometimes program goroutines leak and exit hangs.

ev an: minimal snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter := client.Generator().Stream(ctx, prompt)
go func() {
  for iter.Next() {
    if iter.Value() == "\n" { cancel() }
  }
  log.Println("iterator done")
}()
// process sometimes blocks at exit
```

rita: can you attach pprof? is Err() nil in repro?

ev an: Err() often nil. pprof shows goroutine stuck in read loop around http2 response body Read(). server log shows auth retry exchange then connection close.

sam: UX suggestions: 1) add Close()/Abort() on iterator, 2) make Next() select on provided ctx.Done(), 3) add TryNext() that returns immediately if nothing ready.

rita: prefer Close() as primary: many sample apps use context.Background() so relying on ctx cancellation isn't enough. Close() gives deterministic cleanup.

sam: agree. implementation note: iterator currently hides transport and shares http.Client across generators. Close() must signal read pump and safely close transport for that stream without impacting other streams. maybe per-stream net.Conn wrap or use a context with cancel that ties to stream lifetime.

ev an: I pushed a tiny wrapper that creates a child ctx and exposes Close() which cancels it; works as workaround. will paste gist in the issue.
